caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal Nos. 1024-1031 of 2003
lawyer:
Md Khalilur Rahman, Advocate, instructed by Mvi.  Md Wahidullah, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Petitioners. 
Muniruzzaman, Advocate (appeared with the leave of the Court), instructed by Md Nawab Ali, Advocate-on- Record  ------ For Respondent No. 2.  
Not represented ------ Respondent Nos.1, 3-9. 
Not represented ------ Respondent No. 1.
parties:
Star Jute Mills Ltd ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Chairman, Labour Court, Khulna and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Md Fazlul Karim J: Star Jute Mills Limited represented by its General Manager seeks leave to appeal in these petitions impugning judgment and order dated 6-4-2003 in Writ Petition No.3481 of 2001 heard analogously with Writ Petition Nos.1122-1128 of 2003 by the High Court Division discharging the Rules affirming those dated 21-6- 2001 of the Chairman, Labour Court, Khulna in Complaint Case Nos.51-58 of 2000 heard analogously under section 25(1)(b) of the Employment of Labour (Standing Orders) Act, 1965 allowing reinstatement of the respondent Nos.2-9 with back wages. 

 2. The respondent Nos. 2-9 filed their respective Complaint Case Nos.5158 of 2000 before the Khulna Labour Court against the order of their termination of service passed by the petitioner company stating, inter alia, that they were employed in the petitioner company in different categories as workers and had been serving since their employment in the petitioner company's mills. From the beginning of their service they were involved in Trade Union activities. The respondent No.2 (complainant in Case No.51 of 2001), SM Golam Rahman was an important Trade Unionist. He acted as President of the CBA in 1971, 1987, 1989 and 1994. The other respondents No.3-9 were supporters of Mr SM Golam Rahman. All the said respondents used to take part in Trade Union and used to raise voice against the management of the petitioner for their unlawful activities. 17-3-2001 was Eid-ul-Azha day and before that date the officers and employees were scheduled to get salaries and bonus. But the weekly wages and bonus of the workers were not paid. However, 15-3-2000 was fixed for disbursement of bonus and weekly wages of the workers. But later they were informed that their wages and allowances would not be paid on that day. As a result, the workers become agitated and started procession within the mills area. Later, SM Golam Rahman (respondent No.2) and some other workers and leaders brought the situation under control and the workers on receipt of their payment left the mills premises. At the time when the procession and agitation were going on in the mills premises certain workers started throwing brick-bats towards the houses and office buildings of the petitioner company. As a result the building and residential quarters of the petitioner company were badly damaged due to this unruly incident on 15-3-2000. They further alleged that the mills management thereafter terminated the services of the respondents No.2-9 on 28-3-2000 under section 19(1) of the said Act with all termination benefits. The said termination orders were not a simple termination and amounts to dismissal from service. The management terminated their services to harm and damage the respondents due to their Trade Union activities as its officers. As such, after receipt of the order of termination, the said respondents No.2-9 submitted their grievance petitions to the petitioner company and since no response was received, they filed the aforesaid 8 Complaint Case Nos.51-58 under section 25(1)(b) of the said Act against the petitioner company praying for setting aside the orders of their termination from service and for their reinstatement in service with back wages and other incidental benefits. 

 3. The petitioner company appeared in the said cases arid contested all the cases by filing separate written statement denying the material allegations and stating, inter alia, that the cases of the said respondents were misconceived and not maintainable under section 25(1)(b) of the said Act. The said respondents were simply terminated from their services by orders dated 28-3-2000 under section 19(1) of the said Act with all monetary service benefits as admissible thereunder, without any allegation or blame or stigma. This was a simple termination with all benefits. The said respondents were not at all involved in Trade Union activities. Even the respondent No.2 was not an office-bearer of the Union at the time of his termination of service. The orders of termination from service were not made for their Trade Union activities. In fact, they were not at all connected with any trade union activities nor they were any officers of the Union. Their allegations that they were Trade Union officers were false, incorrect and motivated. The said termination orders were not passed for damaging their Trade Union activities. It was further stated that before Eid-ul-Azha of 2000 (falling on 17-3-2000) an amount of Taka 1,32,00,000 (Taka one crore thirty-two lac) was disbursed to the workers and employees as their wages and allowances. However, since there was some shortage of funds to meet the demands of the workers, some of the over enthusiastic workers and some outsiders started unruly activities, damaged the mills properties, broken the furniture, thrown brick bats heavily, injured the security guards on duty and other employees of the mills, badly damaged the buildings and residential quarters and created a reign of terror in the mills by their violent activities. As a result, the management .lodged a first information report on 19-3-2001 and started a criminal case against 35 accused persons with Digolia PS including 3 of the said respondents. Thereafter, the said respondents were simply terminated from service on- 28-3-2000 with all termination benefits without any blame or stigma or allegation against them and without any reference to the said first information report dated 19-3-2000. These were simple 'termination of service under section 19(1) of the said Act with all monetary benefits as admissible thereunder. Therefore, termination orders there not oriented with any of their alleged or so-called Trade Union activities and that the termination orders were legal and valid. Hence, the cases were not entertain able tinder the proviso of section 19(1) of the said Act. But the said respondents filed the aforesaid cases with false allegations and, as such, the petitioner company prayed for dismissal of the said cases. 

 4. Mr Md Khalilur Rahman, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioners submitted that the High Court Division was carried away by emotion and sentiment in discharging the rules in the above writ petitions mainly basing on 2 unexhibited papers namely, Annexure-X and X-1 filed by the said respondents in the High Court Division. with their supplementary affidavit,' which were neither exhibited in the Labour Court nor filed in the Labour Court nor these were found in the Labour Court records of the cases and, as such, do not constitute any legal evidence and these Annexures X and X-1 ought to have. been kept out of consideration and the High Court Division illegally affirmed the orders of the Labour Court for reinstatement of the respondent Nos. 2-9 in service with all back wages, whom the petitioner company simply terminated from service under section 19(1) of the said Act with all monetary termination benefits as admissible thereunder without assigning any reason or blame or stigma in the interest of the enterprise, which plays a very important role in the national economy, without consideration of the fact that the case was barred under the proviso to section 25(1)(b) of the said Act in view of the fact that they were neither terminated from service for any Trade Union activities nor they were deprived of any benefits for such termination of service under section 19(1) of the said Act. 

 5. Admittedly, the petitioner lodged a, first information report dated 19-3-2000, against the respondent No, 2 and, others alleging certain evidence subversive to discipline and law and order situation occurred on 15-3-2000. It further appears from Annexure-X and X-1 that on 18-3-2000 an enquiry committee was appointed to enquire into the matter of the incidence dated 15-3-2000. The report of the enquiry Annexure-Xvl was submitted on 28-3-2900 and the respondents were terminated on 29-3-2000. Respondent Nos.2-9 have asserted that the respondent No.2 SM Golam Rahman was elected President of CBA for ,4 terms in the years 1971, 1987, 1989 and 1994 and also got elected at present and is the sitting President of the CBA and other respondents are his fellow activists and dissatisfaction arose amongst the workers and laborers with reference to the salaries and bonus payable before Eid-ul-Azaha giving rise to agitation as mentioned above and that the said agitation gave rise to criminal case lodged by the petitioner company with Digolia Polite Station on 19-3-2000 and in order to take revenge, the orders of termination were passed with malafide intention to punish and out the respondents from the Mills. 

 7. Mr Md Khalilur Rahman strenuously argued to find fault with the impugned judgment of the High Court Division relying on the principle enunciated in the case of Secretary, EPIDC vs M Serajul Hoque reported in 25 DLR (SC) 80 and the case of Khulna Newsprint Mills Ltd vs Khulna Newsprint Employees Union reported in 25 DLR (SC) 85 that mere fact that the charge was drawn against the employee earlier is no bar to terminate the employment of the employee by giving him salary in lieu of notice under section 19 of the Employment of Labour (Standing Orders) Act, 1965. In the instant case, both the Courts below have found that in their irresistible opinion it cannot be denied that the occurrence dated 15-3-2000 was behind the issuance of the order of termination or that the actions of the petitioner are due to the trade union activities for the participation of respondent No.2 SM Golam Rahman, the President of the CBA and other office-bearers in the incident dated 15-3-2001. The Labour Court under the provision of section 18 of the Employment of Labour (Standing Orders) Act, 1965 is to see whether the delinquent employee has been dealt with in accordance with law following the principle of natural justice. 

 "In the instant case, it appears from the records including Annexure-X and X(1) that for the occurrence of 15-3-2000 First Information Report was lodged by the Management on 19- 3-2000 and on 22-3-2000 Committee was formed to hold enquiry into the matter and on 28-3-2000 the report of the enquiry committee Annexure-Xil) was submitted and on 29-3- 2000 the termination letters were issued. Before receiving the report of the Enquiry Committee formed by the Management of the petitioner on 22-3-2000, we are at a loss to understand what prompted to Management to issue the orders of termination on 28-3-2000. Though it has persistently been asserted on behalf of the petitioner that there is no stigma or blame on the shoulders of the respondents in the orders of termination but from the facts mentioned above we find substance in the submission of the learned Advocate for the respondents that the said order of termination are aimed at causing harm to the career of the respondents." 

 9. The learned Counsel refers in the case of Karnaphuli Fertiliser Co Ltd vs Chairman, Labour Court, Chittagong reported in 2001 BLD 319 = 56 DLR 502 duly affirmed by this Division for the proposition that first information report is no bar to termination but the fact in that case being different from the present case, the first information report, the report of the enquiry committee and the fact that one of the respondents was the President and the others having participated in the incident dated 15- 3-2000 over which first information report was lodged on 19-3-2000 and the enquiry committee having submitted its report on 28-3-2000 and could not fix any liability on the respondents but the impugned order of termination under section 19 of the Employment of Labour (Standing Orders) Act, 1965 on 29-3-2000 was obviously due to the outcome of the occurrence dated 15-3-2000. 

 10. The finding of fact arrived at by the Courts below on consideration of the material on record do not inspire us to interfere with the impugned judgment of the High Court Division. In the facts and circumstances of the case, we do not find any substance in the submissions of the learned Counsel for the petitioner.
